papers.title: Social media use and adolescent anxiety: a randomised trial in 12 schools, 2019–2021
papers.authors: Michael Kuria, D. Ndetei, Priya Nair, Tom Okafor, et al.
papers.abstract: Background: Heavy social media use has been linked to anxiety in adolescents. Methods: In this randomised trial, 1,200 adolescents aged 13 to 17 from 12 schools were assigned to a four-week reduction programme or to usual use. Anxiety was measured with the GAD-7 at baseline and after 4 weeks. Results: Anxiety scores fell by 2.5 points in the reduction group and by 0.8 points in the control group (p = .003). Conclusions: Cutting social media use for four weeks reduced anxiety.

Abstract: We pooled 21 randomised trials of mindfulness for test anxiety in university students. The pooled effect was moderate, g = 0.52, with high heterogeneity.

a qualitative study. arXiv.
Abstract: Teacher burnout was explored in a qualitative study of 18 secondary school teachers in Kenya using semi-structured interviews. Teachers described long hours, large classes and little support.
